hook: Before Jesus ever performed a single miracle, John calls Him something astonishing: the Word that was with God in the very beginning. Today, John chapter 1.
description: John chapter 1 opens the fourth Gospel with one of the most majestic sentences in Scripture: In the beginning was the Word. In this episode we walk through the whole chapter, from the eternal Word, to the Light that shines in darkness, to the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world, and we see how every part of John 1 points to Jesus. Then we bring it home with three simple ways to live this chapter today.

sections.title: Welcome
sections.narration: Welcome to Biblia Tafsiri Mbalimbali, where we walk through the Bible one chapter a day. Today we arrive at one of the most breathtaking openings in all of Scripture: John chapter 1. Wherever you are listening from, ask God to open your eyes, because this chapter introduces Jesus in a way you may never have considered before.

sections.title: Where We Are in the Story
sections.narration: John's Gospel is the fourth Gospel, written by John the beloved disciple: the fisherman who left his nets to follow Jesus, leaned on His chest at the last supper, and stood at the foot of the cross. While Matthew begins with a family tree and Luke begins in a stable, John reaches all the way back to eternity, deliberately echoing the first words of Genesis: in the beginning. And he writes with one clear purpose, stated near the end of his book: that you might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing, you might have life through His name. Keep that purpose in mind, because everything in this chapter serves it.

sections.title: The Eternal Word
sections.narration: The chapter opens not with a manger, but with eternity. Before anything was created, the Word already was. John calls Jesus the Word, the Logos: God's perfect and final self-expression. Everything God has to say to humanity, He says it in His Son.

sections.title: The Light and the Witness
sections.narration: From eternity, John moves straight into our darkness. The light, he says, shines in darkness, and the darkness cannot overcome it. Into that darkness God sends a witness: John the Baptist, a man sent from God, not to be the light, but to bear witness of the light. Then comes one of the saddest and truest lines in Scripture: He came unto His own, and His own received Him not. The world that His hands had made did not recognize its Maker. But the verse does not end there. To as many as received Him, to them gave He power to become the sons of God. Rejection was real, but reception was possible, and it still is today.
on_screen: John: a witness, not the light

sections.title: The Word Made Flesh
sections.narration: Dwelt among us: in the Greek, He tabernacled among us. He pitched His tent, just as the glory of God once filled the tabernacle in the wilderness. The infinite God stepped into a human body, and the glory the prophets only longed to see, the disciples saw with their own eyes.

sections.title: Come and See
sections.narration: The second half of the chapter turns from heaven to a riverbank. John the Baptist sees Jesus and points: two of his own disciples hear him speak and immediately follow Jesus. One of them, Andrew, runs to find his brother Simon, and brings him to the Lord. The next day Jesus calls Philip, and Philip finds Nathanael under the fig tree. When Nathanael doubts that anything good can come from Nazareth, Philip does not argue; he simply offers the best invitation in the Bible: come and see. And Jesus, seeing Nathanael's honest heart, promises him something greater: he will see heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.
on_screen: Angels on the Son of Man

sections.title: The Lamb of God
sections.narration: One sentence holds the entire gospel: a Lamb, provided by God, sacrificed, and not merely covering sin, but taking it away. Every Passover lamb, every sacrifice on every altar, was pointing here.

sections.title: Seeing Jesus in John 1
sections.narration: This chapter is Jesus from its first word to its last. He is the Word, eternal and divine. He is the Light that darkness cannot overcome. He is the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth. He is the Lamb of God, fulfilling every sacrifice since Abel's flock and Abraham's substitute on Mount Moriah. And when Jesus calls Himself the Son of Man and promises that angels will ascend and descend upon Him, He is quietly claiming the ladder from Jacob's dream at Bethel: He Himself is the stairway between heaven and earth, the bridge a holy God walks to reach sinners like us. John 1 is not merely introducing a teacher or a prophet. It is announcing that God has come, and His name is Jesus.
on_screen: The Word · the Light · the Lamb

sections.title: Living It Today
sections.narration: So how do we carry John chapter 1 into an ordinary Tuesday? First, receive Him. The chapter says as many as received Him became sons of God, so before your feet touch the floor tomorrow morning, greet the Lord first and give Him the first word of your day. Second, bear witness like John the Baptist. He was not the light, and he never tried to be; he simply pointed beyond himself with humility. You do not need to be a preacher to do that. Point someone to Jesus today by your kindness, your honesty, and one honest sentence about why you have hope. Third, come and see. Philip did not win an argument with Nathanael; he extended an invitation. Invite one person this week to read the Gospel of John with you, or simply to watch along with this journey chapter by chapter, and let Jesus make the introduction Himself.
on_screen: Invite one person: come and see

sections.title: Until Tomorrow
sections.narration: May the Word who was in the beginning speak into your day today, and may the Light shine into every dark corner of it. Tomorrow we continue with John chapter 2, where water becomes wine at a wedding in Cana. Subscribe and join us tomorrow, same time, one chapter a day, through the whole Bible.
